query: US-Iran conflict status July 2026: is there a ceasefire in effect? Latest on Islamabad MoU, tit-for-tat strikes, Trump statements, negotiations after July 11 2026
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

**No ceasefire is in effect as of mid-July 2026.** The ceasefire formalized by the **Islamabad Memorandum** (signed June 17, 2026, establishing a 60-day negotiation window) collapsed after roughly three weeks:

- **July 8**: Trump declared the ceasefire/MoU "over" after Iran struck commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the US retaliated.
- **July 11**: US hit ~140 Iranian targets after a ship attack.
- **July 13**: Iran formally announced it would no longer comply with the MoU, accusing the US of "openly violating it."
- **July 14**: US reinstated its naval blockade.
- **July 15-16**: US conducting daily airstrikes (sixth consecutive night by July 16); Iran retaliating against US allies (Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan).

**Core dispute**: Conflicting interpretations of the Strait of Hormuz clauses in the 14-point memorandum—Iran wanted to charge fees/retain authority; the US insisted on an open, toll-free waterway.

**Negotiations after July 11**: No active talks. Iran's Foreign Ministry said "no plans for negotiations" (July 15). Mediation by Qatar, Pakistan, and Oman continues but has not restarted formal negotiations. Trump's July 16 primetime address claimed the US is "winning big in Iran" while threatening more strikes unless Tehran returns to talks.

All findings are cross-validated across CNN live coverage (July 10-16), Wikipedia, Al Jazeera, NPR, Axios, and the UK House of Commons Library, and delivered via the structured output tool with 15 key facts, 14 quantitative data points, and 15 sources.

key_facts: There is NO ceasefire in effect as of mid-July 2026; Trump declared the ceasefire/Islamabad Memorandum 'over' on July 8, 2026.

The Islamabad Memorandum was signed June 17, 2026 by Trump (at Versailles post-G7) and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian (in Tehran); it was a 14-point framework establishing a 60-day negotiation window.
The MoU was primarily brokered by Pakistan, with Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Egypt facilitating; it was digitally signed June 14-15, 2026.

MoU terms: end to strikes, toll-free reopening of Strait of Hormuz for 60 days, end of US naval blockade, 60-day sanctions waiver, and (subject to final deal) a $300B+ investment fund plus frozen asset release.
The MoU deferred the nuclear issue: no accord on Iran's nuclear program or uranium stockpiles; only a call to downgrade uranium from weapons-grade to reactor-grade after a final deal.
Ceasefire collapsed after ~3 weeks; on July 8 Iran struck commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and the US retaliated on Iranian territory.
On July 13, 2026 Iran's Foreign Ministry (spokesperson Esmail Baghaei) announced Iran would no longer comply with the MoU because the US was 'openly violating it.'
Core dispute: conflicting interpretation of Strait of Hormuz clauses — Iran sought to charge fees/retain authority; US insisted on an open toll-free waterway.
As of July 16, 2026 the US conducted its sixth consecutive night of airstrikes; targets included southern Iran, Greater Tunb and Hengam Islands, Bandar Abbas, Ahvaz, and bridges/power lines/railways.
US reinstated its naval blockade on July 14, 2026; Strait of Hormuz traffic dropped to ~3 ships per 24 hours (July 16) vs ~110/day normally.
Iran retaliated by striking US infrastructure in Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan and claimed strikes on US forces at al-Tanf, Syria.
No active negotiations as of July 15-16; Iran's Foreign Ministry said 'no plans for negotiations'; mediation by Qatar, Pakistan and Oman continues.
US strikes over the prior week reportedly killed at least 35 and wounded ~300 (Iranian health officials); July 15-16 Iranian figures cite 30+ civilians killed, 260+ injured.
Trump's July 16 primetime address said the US is 'winning big in Iran'; he threatened to strike Iranian bridges and power plants unless Tehran returns to talks.
Only 29% of Americans approve of Trump's handling of the Iran conflict (Washington Post-Ipsos poll, ~July 16, 2026).
Sources reference Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei (indicating a succession from Ali Khamenei in this scenario) who endorsed the MoU despite misgivings.
